column.text: Binance's $6.3B exploit is the one thing that matters this Friday, and it is why longs got flushed. Reportedly tied to North Korea's Lazarus Group through a compromised engineer laptop, the hack helped drive $351M in long liquidations against just $54M in shorts. That is forced deleveraging, not a wave of organic selling, and it is the mechanism we are trading. Price has absorbed it so far. BTC sits at $77,487 with RSI at 34.6, and Fear & Greed is at 30. ETH is the weak link after breaking below $2,200. Flows split the market. On Thursday 29 Oct, BTC ETFs took in $17.1M, lifting the seven-day net to $195.7M. ETH ETFs lost $105.5M that same day, leaving a seven-day net outflow of $366.9M. SOL ETFs shed $27.7M on Thursday 29 Oct, with a seven-day net of −$68.7M. Bitcoin has institutional demand underneath it. Ether does not. Backstops are real. Binance says it has $6.34 billion ready to cover losses, and Tether and Circle have frozen between $2.1B and $2.41B of the stolen funds. Still, dollar liquidity is flat, so there is no macro tailwind to lean on. The regime is risk-off, but a down-trending tape is not a short signal by itself. Do not chase the breakdown, and do not reflexively buy the dip. A counter-trend long needs clear support, a real catalyst, and evidence of reversal. Any short needs a mechanism you can point to in the printed data, and below conviction 7 it trades at half size. Watch whether $76k holds while ETF inflows persist. A clean break there keeps the sellers in control.
